After hearing about the new policies going into affect it makes me wonder if this won't get much much worse. 

And if I even tried to be specific or upset I'm sure I'd be labeled as the bad guy. So who knows. I guess just have to take "buyer beware" to consideration.

Decent study place close to campus. Relatively large seating area with outdoor options as well. My experience in store have usually been excellent, as far as customer service, drink quality/consistency, and ambience, but I can't say the same about drive-thru. Several times I have gone through and my order was wrong-like, completely wrong to the point of being undrinkable, and I'm not that picky when it comes to coffee, lol. I was able to contact Starbucks for refunds to my Starbucks Rewards account, but it was still annoying to not have a drink after making time before work to grab one. The concotions included: iced green tea with a splace of milk in it instead of a green tea latte; fruity green tea with cinnamon syrup; and a venti latte with 4 extra shots of ESPRESSO instead of sweetner (at a significant upcharge and unpleasant taste, lol). As for merchandise, I'd say that the general quality of Starbucks' ceramic coffee cups and water bottles has declined. The print pattern peeled off the water bottle within a week of use, and the ceramic cup cracked when I poured hot water in it for tea.

Been going their for years until the other day,gave me a toasted bagel with mold
Very disgusted

Typical Starbucks exceptional staff. Cleanest public bathroom anywhere. Like all stores, the menu is the same as all the others. Sit outside on a nice day, inside is on the small side, but comfortable.
Super friendly staff! I ordered a complicated drink and they made sure they made it right.  Super cute store.

I love Starbucks cold brew, but definitely into the pumpkin cold brew right now. I'm going to be honest and say that if there were a local coffee shop near this Starbucks (which is by my work) I would definitely go to the local shop because I'm 100% supporting small business. However, Starbucks is a lot closer to my work and just convenient. This one is fairly small so it does get kind of loud unless you can find seating outside

My first review of a Starbucks.  As a shareholder and frequent traveler, I use SB as my default coffee place.  Mostly for the consistent product and ease of access.    Anyway, I was excited to move to Tucson and have a Starbucks within a mile of my house.   I have been frequenting this particular SB 5 days a week for three months.  I have to say,  I absolutely stopped going.    Here's why...........

1.  I can wait at the front counter like an idiot for 30 seconds to a minute with no one greeting me, looking at me, or helping me.  Doesn't sound like much,  but seems like an eternity when you have 5 staff just walking past you.

2.  After three months, over 180 visits,   same order every time.   Every Time.       They act like they've never seen me before.   "Do you want cream with that?"   Yes.   Like the other hundred plus times. FYI: Grande Pike with lil room.  Not too tuff.

3.  They have dropped off my coffee at the counter,  not looking at me or saying anything and just keep walking by.  No ty, have a nice day, here you go.....   wow.

So... yesterday I go to Ina and Orange Grove SB.  Walk into the front door.  "HI Guys!  What can I get you?".

Day two.....  "Welcome Back!"

Found my new Starbucks.

It's worth the extra .5 mile walk.    I do miss the nice porch and the guy that drives a Harley and listens to his headphones every morning.

Extremely friendly staff. This is only my second time here, and the guy taking my order remembered me and my obsession with Peppermint Mocha.

Orders come up quickly. Nice sized space with plenty of tables for dining or working. Outdoor space and clean facilities.

There is not much indoor seating, and when I arrived on a rainy day (so the patio wasn't an option), I had doubts about whether I'd get a seat. Luckily, a group left soon after. When I approached the register, all three employees were engaged in conversation and it took a while before one of them could be bothered to help me. At least she was friendly. My drink was a little slow to be prepared and for a frappuccino, it tasted kind of watery/icy.

Internet was okay but it went out for a tiny bit.

Wasn't too happy about the restroom being closed.

It's Starbucks - if you haven't heard of this place, congratulations. You're a Bona Fide hermit!

That said, this location had confusing signage and ordering.  I know they had more options to choose from, but they had a small board with small cross-section of selections.

Also, the Carmel Macchiato I ordered didn't taste very strong at all.  The get a better coffee at Dunkin' Donuts, and it's cheaper.

For the amount of people working there it seemed like only 1 was truly making the coffees, so it took forever.

Gonna pass on this location in the future...

Great location 

Atmosphere: very spacious and open. Comfortable seating

I ordered my usual half passion half black iced tea unsweetened. It was perfect. 

They have plastic sippy cups now. I think it's great that they are cutting back on using plastic straws.

This location is awesome. The staff is consistently friendly and the best part is this place has a bunch of comfortable places to sit, and tons of outlets. 

There's almost always a shortage of outlets at any cafe but this spot has you covered.

Also I just like the way Starbucks tastes. I can get a cold brew for $3.19 here where at the Well down the street they're $5.

I understand they are some kind of nonprofit but for a small cold brew that just feels too high. We're not at an airport or movie theatre sheesh.

Came before 8am. Great service at the register but terribly slow at making the drink. I ordered an iced green tea. I waited over ten minutes. Will go out of my way to another location versus coming here.

Update! Came to get a drink because my new office is nearby and they were quick about drunk making but the barista didn't charge me correctly, sigh!

This is my least favorite Starbucks in the city.  Forget about it if you are in any kind of a hurry. While you are waiting in line, craving your caffeine rush before you face your workday, and the person in front of you orders a grande Pike Place that, for some reason, takes two people two minutes to prepare and ring up, you will wish that the Oracles were there to shoot you with their laser eyes, and put you out of your misery.
