Overall, your experience at any given Starbucks mainly depends on the quality of any given barista that may make your order; the food and drinks are consistently pretty darned good across any of the chain's locations that you may visit. And for this first visit, my greet tea Frappuccino is as delicious as any that I have gotten before at other Starbucks.

So let's talk about what is unique about this particular Starbucks location.

Starbucks moved to this much more spacious location, formerly a nice Cosi, from the smaller one it had across the street at 1201 Walnut. Starbucks leveled the entire floor, from the step-up dining area that the former Cosi had. This is a great location within Philadelphia's bustling "Gayborhood", through which a lot of customers funnel throughout the day.

There is plenty of space to move around within the restaurant, which actually is the one big fault I have of it. There is not an ample amount of seating here, especially when you take the cavernous size of available space here into consideration. Starbucks could easily seat many more people, if it bought more tables & chairs to reconfigure a denser dining area. I was here just before the dinner hour on a Sunday, and I was lucky someone moved so I could have a seat.

The restroom area is sizable, and interesting that each restroom does not have sinks inside them - the hand-washing sink area is on the outside of each restroom. It's a pretty cool setup, until you consider that you will be touching other people's urine and feces on the door handle when you exit the room. Having the sinks on the outside of the restroom is fine, if you have door-less walk-in restrooms (which this location does not have). So there's that.

There doesn't seem to be any outdoor seating, and the weather has been nice for the past few weeks that this location has been open. Cosi used to have to deal with a lot of less desirable types of people lingering with its outdoor seating; perhaps Starbucks just doesn't want to deal with that element at all, by forgoing outdoor tables and chairs?

Otherwise, Starbucks should be applauded for moving to this larger location. It should allow greater amounts of people to get in and out quicker.

This location closes at 9 pm. I got in their line that was wrapped around the building at 8:38 pm. I made it to the order window at 9:03 and was told they were closed and wouldn't take my order despite me having been in their line for almost half an hour. I was honestly stunned at how poor their service is. Maybe take a class from Chick-Fil-A. They can move their line efficiently, and would never refuse service. Absolutely horrible service.

Haven't been to this Starbucks in a very long time. Not because I don't like it here but just because I havent had time. Also I am not a big fan of the parking lot lol this is why I park where the Snack Shack (shhhh) 

I ordered the CARAMEL BRULEE with extra BRULEE (of course)

The customer service here is great!! I am pretty sure the Starbucks employee's name was Bret? He was energetic considering I was half asleep and needed my coffee lol but he made me want to come back.. Which I will! 

There is also a side door you can walk out of, which is just a short walk back to Snack Shack where I parked my car. Also near the side door is where all the goodies are such as the vanilla, cup sleeves, stirrers and napkins. If they are low on anything let an employee know they are very helpful and always smiling.Ill be back soon.

Fair service-  messed up my drink cuppa times.  Nice folks but staff isn't well trained.  Kind clean- kinda dirty.  I'd say find a different coffee shop if u want quality-  only use this place in a pinch

On my way out of Reno last week I noted a new Starbucks by the Hampton Inn at the I-80 W on-ramp. I was HAPPY because I was going to have to have gas station coffee after noting the old Starbucks at Raley's had shuttered. Nothing stays the same! 

My standard order 1 grande hot latte, turned out perfect, my Dad was with me and I got him a tall latte which he said was great. Espresso was hot and came out quickly. I was caffeinated and ready to head up the hill for my trip home. 

My only complaint is that I was trying to look at the display case at snack options and the focus from an employee was refilling the case and I felt like I was in the way. I ended up not getting anything other than coffee. I'm not someone who insists on special treatment as a customer- I know it's super hard to keep all the ducks in a row when multitasking and you are serving people but a good point for a manager to pick up on and mention that without customers we wouldn't have a job...give them some space. 

They have a drive-in that looks like it gets a lot of traction. Great addition to the area and smooth access in and out.

always closing drive thru. i've driven here so many times and have to find another one bc i specifically was not going to get down. first world problems i know but it is very annoying when it happens so often i'm not sure what the problem is i hope it's not laziness.

This is now one of two Starbucks in the shopping district (another inside Fry's). Being my closest Starbucks, I have come here numerous times for a hot cup of Joe. There's some seating outside and it's small inside, but it's a Starbucks, so you know what you are getting. Never had a complaint or any issues, just hot coffee and tea!

Besides it being super busy often, usually, I really like this location. The employees are friendly and they make the hot matcha green tea well (which is not consistently the case for all locations). However, lately my grande orders have been kind of skeet. Maybe only 3/4th of the way full. I don't typically make a big deal about it when it happens here and there but it's starting to become a trend and we all know Starbucks isn't cheap. Still a hopeful customer for now, though!
